newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter won't underwrite NC bonds - official.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter won't underwrite NC bonds - official.

text.p: Dean Witter Reynolds Inc will not do negotiated bond underwritings for the state of North Carolina for the next two years because an employee inadvertently made a political contribution to a state official, a firm spokesperson said.
"Dean Witter is voluntarily not doing any municipal (underwriting) business in North Carolina," Suzanne Platenic, vice president of media relations at the firm said in a telephone interview.

Dean Witter disclosed the contribution in a quarterly report to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board as required by the board's "pay-to-play" rule G-37. Quarterly reports were due at MSRB on October 31.

The report, obtained by Reuters, says the firm got a "refund" in September of a contribution that one of its employees inadvertently made last quarter to a "North Carolina official." The report does not identify the state official or who at Dean Witter made the contribution.

But Brian Devlin, senior vice president for Dean Witter, said earlier today: "It had nothing to do with the municipal division. It was another area of the firm. Someone inadvertently made a contribution to North Carolina, which we felt could have violated rule G-37."
Rule G-37 bars muni dealers who make contributions to issuer clients from doing negotiated bond business for two years with those governments.
Platenic said earlier today that the firm caught the contribution in a routine audit of employee contributions.

A spokesman for Rauscher Pierce Refsnes, Inc told Reuters on Thursday that the firm will refrain from negotiated bond underwriting for the town of Azle, Texas in the coming months because of a $150 contribution by an employee before that employee came on board at the firm.
